messages.subject: Re: Renjin, Gradle, and Google App Engine
messages.subject_clean: Renjin, Gradle, and Google App Engine
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ivan,
You probably want to use a more recent release of Renjin, which is
perhaps confusingly, 0.7.1548, but other than that, your Gradle
configuration looks fine.

However, in order to run in the AppEngine environment, you will need
to create your ScriptEngine using the AppEngineContextFactory, which
helps you create a Session that is configured to be AppEngine-safe.
Otherwise the ScriptEngine initialization will fail silently when shot
down by the gae sandbox.

See the example here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-examples/blob/master/appengine-servlet/src/main/java/org/renjin/example/appengine/RenjinServlet.java

Does that help?
Alex

On Tue, Aug 4, 2015 at 11:28 AM,  <ivan....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm having some trouble getting the code in the documentation
> (http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/introduction.html#setting-up-a-java-project-for-renjin)
> working. When I attempt to getEngineByName, on my local development server,
> the returned engine is null. However, the engine is returned correctly
> during my unit tests. I assumed that this because the Renjin jars are
> missing from my CLASSPATH on the dev server while being present for my jUnit
> tests. This does turn out to be the case when I print the CLASSPATH in both
> situations.
>
> Is there something I'm missing to get the CLASSPATH to be populated
> correctly on the dev server? I'm using Gradle as my build system. This is
> how I'm declaring Renjin as a dependency:
>
> repositories {
>     maven { url "http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/" }
> }
>
>
> ...
>
> dependencies {
>     compile group: 'org.renjin', name: 'renjin-appengine',
> version:'0.7.0-RC8-SNAPSHOT'
> }
>
>
> Here is the sample of App Engine code that runs correctly but only in a
> jUnit test:
>
> public RResponse runFunction(@Named("function") String function) {
>     RResponse response = new RResponse();
>
>     ScriptEngineManager manager = new ScriptEngineManager();
>     ScriptEngine engine = manager.getEngineByName("Renjin");
>
>     /* This is how I checked the CLASSPATH */
>     System.out.println(System.getProperty("java.class.path"));
>
>     try {
>         engine.eval(function); /* NullPointerException is thrown here */
>         response.setCode("SUCCESS");
>     } catch (ScriptException e) {
>         response.setCode("FAILURE");
>         response.setReason(e.getMessage());
>     }
>
>     return response;
> }
>
>
> Is there something special that I need to do to get this working in a Google
> Cloud Endpoint API?
>
> Thanks!
> Ivan
>

messages.subject: Re: xts objects in renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rob,
It looks like xts uses the .Call interface to C code, which we haven't
fully emulated yet. I'm doing some work on this presently but haven't
yet finished. In the meantime, you should be able to see which
functions depend or don't on native code from the results of the
package examples, but for some reason these haven't yet be tested by
packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org>. I'll see if I can start another build to get you
some more detailed results.

Best,
Alex

On Mon, Aug 3, 2015 at 12:18 PM, Rob Terpilowski
<robterp...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm attempting to create an xts object in Renjin using the as.xts function,
> however I'm getting the following error:
>
> Could not find class for 'native' methods for package 'xts'
> (className='org.renjin.cran.xts.xts')
>
> The code I am using to build the xts object is below.  From the xts
> dependency page I see the following statement:
> This package can be used with Renjin but there was an error compiling
> C/Fortran sources and no tests could be found for the package.
>
> How can I tell which function in the xts package are using C/Fortran
> sources, and does this mean I'm SOL trying to use XTS objects in my
> application?
>
> Thanks,
> -Rob
>
>
>         engine.eval("library(xts)");
>         engine.eval("library(zoo)");
>         ListVector.Builder classListBuilder = ListVector.newBuilder();
>
>         DoubleVector dv = new DoubleArrayVector(22);
>         DoubleVector dv2 = new DoubleArrayVector(4);
>
>         StringVector sv = new StringArrayVector("2010-05-05");
>         classListBuilder.setDim(1, 3);
>         classListBuilder.set(0, sv);
>         classListBuilder.set(1, dv);
>         classListBuilder.set(1, dv);
>         ListVector lv = classListBuilder.build();
>         engine.put("sv", sv);
>         engine.put("lv", lv);
>
>         engine.eval("df <- data.frame(as.Date(sv), lv)");
>         engine.eval("names(df)[1] <- \"Date\"");
>         engine.eval("my.xts <- xts(df[,2], order.by <http://order.by>=df$Date)");
>         Object eval = engine.eval("print(my.xts)");
>         System.out.println("Eval: " + eval);
>
>

messages.subject: is 'stringr' really supported ?
messages.body_plain:
Per your package docs it looks like Renjin supports the "stringr" package, but I get the runtime exception below. It looks like the jvm is trying to find a native library, which contradicts your 100% java implementation. Please advise. Thanks.

Exception in thread "main" org.renjin.eval.EvalException: Could not find class for 'native' methods for package 'stringi' (className='org.renjin.cran.stringi.stringi')
at org.renjin.primitives.Native.getPackageClass(Native.java:324)
at org.renjin.primitives.Native.dotCall(Native.java:268)
at org.renjin.primitives.R$primitive$$Call.apply(R$primitive$$Call.java:60)
